definition: NNI (Neural Network Intelligence) is a free and open-source AutoML toolkit developed by Microsoft.
details: It is used to automate feature engineering, model compression, neural architecture search, and hyper-parameter tuning. The source code is licensed under MIT License and available on GitHub.

explainer.lead: NNI is a free, open-source AutoML toolkit from Microsoft that automates the fiddly parts of building models. It matters because it packages tuning, architecture search and compression into one reusable tool.

tiers.eli5: It's like an autopilot for the boring parts of building a model, trying many settings for you instead of you doing it by hand.
tiers.practitioner: Teams use it to sweep hyper-parameters and search architectures across many trials, and to compress models for deployment. A pitfall is that broad automated searches can burn a lot of compute if you don't bound the search space.
tiers.paperLevel: NNI is defined as a free and open-source AutoML toolkit; its scope covers feature engineering, model compression, neural architecture search and hyper-parameter tuning. It is licensed under the MIT License and hosted on GitHub.

explainer.example: An engineer configures a hyper-parameter search over learning rate and depth, and NNI runs the trials and reports the best configuration.
